recipes.name: Mushroom Chicken in Sour Cream Sauce
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Mix the salt, pepper, paprika, lemon pepper, and garlic powder together in a bowl; rub evenly onto all sides of the chicken breasts. Place the seasoned chicken into the bottom of a slow cooker. Add the cream of mushroom soup, sour cream, white wine, and mushrooms to the slow cooker.
Secure the cover onto the slow cooker and cook on Low for 8 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Mushroom Chicken in Sour Cream Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Chicken breasts seasoned with paprika, lemon pepper, and garlic powder are slow cooked with white wine, sour cream, mushrooms, and cream of mushroom soup in this easy-to-prepare recipe that cooks while you go about your day.
raw_recipe.name: Mushroom Chicken in Sour Cream Sauce
recipeIngredient: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

recipeInstructions.text: Mix the salt, pepper, paprika, lemon pepper, and garlic powder together in a bowl; rub evenly onto all sides of the chicken breasts. Place the seasoned chicken into the bottom of a slow cooker. Add the cream of mushroom soup, sour cream, white wine, and mushrooms to the slow cooker.
Secure the cover onto the slow cooker and cook on Low for 8 hours.

review.reviewBody: I noticed some of the reviewers thought this was bland, so, I thought I would adjust the seasonings to be more flavorful. I used 4 chicken breasts instead of 6. I doubled all components of the rub except for the salt. I kept it at the same measurement. I heavily sprinkled the chicken breasts with the rub. I also sauteed the mushrooms in a little butter until they were golden brown before adding to the crock pot. This adds additional flavor. I did not add the sour cream at first because I did not want it to curdle or clump. I mixed the soup, chardonnay, mushrooms and covered the chicken. I cooked for 3 hours in the sauce. I then removed the chicken breasts and whisked the sour cream into the sauce until fully incorporated. I then added the chicken breasts back into the sauce and cooked for an additional hour. Boneless chicken breasts definitely do not need 8 hours to cook or they will be dry. The sauce was thick and very flavorful. The chicken was moist and delicious. I served with Jasmine rice and broccoli. Very simple to make and tasty! I'll definitely make again.

The chicken with the rub is definitely not bland. I took the advice of other reviewers and sauteed the mushrooms in a little butter before adding to the pot and I added the sour cream 30 minutes before serving. I also cut the chicken into bite size pieces and put back in the pot after adding the sour cream. My family really liked it. I will definitely be making this again. I had 2 lbs. chicken breast that I cut horizontally across before adding the rub so my breast were thinner and it only took like 3 1/2 hours total to cook. The last half hour I turned it up to high. Served over slightly buttered Jasmine rice. I did double the sauce which does make a lot. Unless you really want a lot of sauce I wouldn't recommend it. Because I doubled the sauce I also doubled the mushrooms. The next day I grilled up some more chicken with the same rub and added to the sauce and served for dinner again. It was very tasty. Thanks wx2computers for sharing a simple and easy but great recipe. UPDATE: The next time we made this my husband threw some of the leftover spice set from the rub (he made a little extra) into the finished sauce and stirred it all together. The extra spices added even more delicious flavor to this dish.

YUM! Absolutely delicious. My husband emphasized I needed to keep track of this recipe for future use. :) And said it would be great for when we have company. The only thing I did differently was I didn't make it in the slow-cooker.

I browned the chicken in a saucepan with some olive oil, butter (just a bit of each) and garlic, as well as the spices mentioned. Then I removed the chicken to a glass pan and put it in the oven at 350. Then I sauteed the mushrooms in the same pan (more garlic and a bit more butter), then added the liquids. I let this simmer on low for about 15-20 minutes while the chicken cooked in the oven. Then, I transferred the sauce onto the chicken and let it cook another 25 minutes or so in the oven. I served it on a bed of rice, with a side of roasted asparagus. YUM YUM YUM! The wine's definitely the key ingredient.

Based on feedback and a distant memory of something similar from my childhood, I made a number of changes. I used 2 huge chicken breasts that I split in half lengthwise. I used a can of cream of mushroom, a can of cream of chicken, 3 cups of sliced white mushrooms sauteed in butter and canola, one diced yellow onion sauteed in canola oil, salt and pepper on both and increased the wine to 3/4 cup. I also added 2 tsp fresh thyme leaves and the seasoning for the chicken was rubbed in garlic powder, Johnny's seasoning salt and fresh ground pepper. As others have mentioned cooking time was drastically shorter and I didn't add the sour cream until the last 1/2 hour. I served it with white rice steamed in chicken broth with butter and fresh steamed broccoli. Very popular at my house.

This recipe was great. I got the small can of Campbell's cream of mushroom w/reduced sodium. Didn't use sour cream and used chicken thighs. I doubled up all the spices except salt like the other reviewer recommended. I pan fried the chicken on both sides in garlic (30 seconds each side) along with half of the dry rub and then put it in slow cooker for 2 hours. Found the sauce too thin so added 2 tablespoons of all purpose flour to thicken it. My slow cooker goes to warm mode after the timer goes off so not sure if that's what made the sauce thin.

I served it with pasta and it was great. I have enough sauce remaining for another dinner so I've frozen it till the next time.

This came out absolutely delicious and I made a few changes based on other reviews so I gave it 4 stars only because I made changes. I doubled the spices listed (except the salt did put in extra but not doubled) and poked the chicken rub with a fork lots of places to get the spice rub in there. I added a little bit of cayenne for a bit of kick. I mixed the soup and sour cream and wine all together then put in. I was out of white wine and used Marsala wine instead. Cooked in crockpot for 4 hours on low. Pull apart tender and delicious. Next time I make it I will probably add an extra can of soup to make more sauce.

I browned the chicken just lightly bc I wanted that golden color and flavor. I doubled spices also, and added sage, thyme, allspice, nutmeg, and marjoram. Basically poultry seasoning if you have that handy. Smoked paprika tripled, and of course added minced garlic to the soup. I added cream of chicken soup as well bc the chicken wasn't covered completely. It's delicious!

I butterflied and flattened each breast adding salt and garlic then browned. Removed from skillet (keeping warm) and combined all the rest of the ingredients into the skillet and whipped well over medium heat. Added chicken back to the skillet and cooked on medium for 15min. Served over white rice. Thanks for this it is wonderful.

Tasty, but I admit I made a lot of changes. I used frozen chicken breasts, put them in the crock pot first, then topped with sliced mushrooms. Then I mixed the rest of the ingredients together and poured it over the top. I swapped out the sour cream for fat free plain yogurt, used healthy soup to cut some calories, and doubled the spices (except for the salt). Easy and healthy dinner.

I followed this simple and delicious recipe except that I made my own cream of mushroom soup from a recipe I found on Pinterest and I cooked it for 30-40 minutes, covered at 350F. It was not at all bland- tasty and delicious!!! Try it with a homemade soup recipe to avoid the MSG, sodium and other questionable ingredients- just butter, flour, milk, mushrooms and garlic* and onion* (*optional) for a healthier option.

I thought this dish was great and so did my family. The chicken was so juicy and not dry at all, I used 5 boneless skinless breasts and cooked on low for 10 hours (the whole time we were at work). The only changes I made was adding extra spices, not adding the sour cream until I got home which was right before we ate and partially shreaded the chicken. I served with wild rice and artichokes...it was a Great dinner that I will make again.
We loved this!! I made a few changes due to our dietary needs which are in my notes. This is going to be a regular in my recipes!!! Thanks for the AMAZING recipe!!!!
fantastic. I added curry once and a moroccan spice another time.

I first tried this pretty much as in the recipe, and I didn't really like the paprika in the sauce. The chicken, however, was delicious in and of itself. The second time, I skipped the paprika, but the sauce tasted pretty bland. Also, the alcohol didn't get cooked out of the wine, and I really didn't like tasting that in my sauce. It was bad enough that my husband actually threw out his dinner. Oh well. At least I tried something new!

Definitely double up on the spices amounts, and like others have suggested, sour cream goes in 30-60 minutes at the end. I marinated mine overnight so I let it cook a long time on low, about 6 or 7 hours and it still came out very juicy.
Tasted great. Converted it to stove top and oven, though. Next time added garlic to the recipe, tasted even better.
I made it twice so far, but not with the mushrooms, since no on in my family likes it. I used 1.5 lbs of chicken. Everyone loved it!

This was delicious. I did omit the sour cream and doubled up on the cream of mushroom and wine. It was great because I had 1lb of leftover diced up cooked chicken I was going to use to make a mexican dish but wanted something else. This was perfect and easy. I also added extra garlic.

This was a quick prep and a tasty, simple meal for summer slow cooking. I followed the recipe closely on the chicken seasoning, but thought the sauce needed a little doctoring so I added some lemon pepper, lemon juice , worchestershire sauce and salt. Served over kluski noodles. Sincere thanks for sharing your recipe.

I cooked it for 4 hours on low and then shredded the chicken and put it back into the crock pot and shut it off. It came out perfect. The sauce was wonderful served over rice. This is a great meal for any busy family.
